jobs.title: Associate Scientist, Vaccines Upstream Bioprocess Development
jobs.location: United States - New York - Pearl River
jobs.description: Use Your Power for Purpose Pfizer’s purpose is to deliver breakthroughs that change patients’ lives. At the core of fulfilling this purpose is Research and Development, where we strive to translate advanced science and technologies into the therapies and vaccines that matter most. Your role will focus on developing robust, scalable, and high-productivity cell culture processes for manufacturing biological therapeutics for both early- and late-phase clinical programs. Your extensive experience and deep understanding of the principles, concepts, and practices of the discipline will make you an invaluable team member. Your expertise will guide critical decision-making processes, often requiring you to choose among limited options. You will actively contribute to all team discussions, bringing your innovative scientific mindset to the table. This proactive approach will help Pfizer achieve new milestones and make a significant impact on patients worldwide. Role Summary The Associate Scientist will contribute to the design, development, and optimization of microbial fermentation processes that support vaccine development within the Upstream Development group in Early Bioprocess Development, Vaccine Research and Development, located in Pearl River, NY. The role will primarily support programs focused on subunit protein vaccines derived from bacterial expression systems, with opportunities to contribute to mammalian cell culture programs as needed. Key responsibilities include screening microbial strains, developing and optimizing fermentation processes, supporting process scale-up, analyzing experimental data, and collaborating with cross-functional partners. The successful candidate will bring a foundation in biochemical engineering, biochemistry, biotechnology, microbiology, or a related discipline and will join a collaborative team dedicated to advancing microbial and mammalian process development for vaccine production. Role Responsibilities In this role, you will: Support the design, development, and optimization of microbial fermentation processes for vaccine antigen production Assist with screening and evaluation of microbial strain candidates using high-throughput fermentation systems Operate fermentation systems up to 75 L scale, including media preparation, fermenter setup, process monitoring and control, and product harvest Perform fermentation sample analysis using high-performance liquid chromatography, bioanalyzers, and other analytical instruments Evaluate and implement new technologies that enhance fermentation process development capabilities within the group Analyze fermentation data and prepare clear summaries for supervisors and cross-functional project teams Document experiments in electronic laboratory notebooks in a timely, accurate, and compliant manner Provide occasional support for mammalian cell culture activities, including bioreactor setup, process monitoring, sampling, and data analysis, as program needs require Flexible work schedule required to support time-sensitive fermentation and cell culture experiments, including occasional work outside of core business hours and on weekends Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements) Bachelor’s degree in Microbiology, Biochemistry, Chemical/Biochemical Engineering, Biotechnology, or a related discipline Familiarity with the design and execution of microbial fermentation and/or mammalian cell culture experiments Solid understanding of microbiology, cell physiology, and biochemical engineering principles Experience operating high-throughput bioreactor systems and benchtop or sterilize-in-place fermenters Ability to complete familiar tasks with limited instruction and supervision Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment Ability to compile, organize, and analyze large data sets using commercial data analytics tools (e.g. Spotfire, Power BI, etc.) Experience preparing and delivering clear scientific summary presentations Bonus Points If You Have (Preferred Requirements) Experience with analytical techniques such as quantitative PCR, Western blot, HPLC, Octet General knowledge of Good Laboratory Practices (part of GxP)/Good Manufacturing Practices (also cGMP) practices Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously Experience using common AI tools, including generative technologies such as Microsoft Copilot or Gemini, to support problem solving and enhance productivity. Demonstrated curiosity for exploring how AI tools can improve outcomes and understanding of responsible practices, including risk management and ethical use PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS This role has no special physical requirements beyond those typically associated with laboratory work, including the ability to occasionally lift 20–30 lb items, perform aseptic transfers, and carry out relevant laboratory functions. Mental requirements include a detailed understanding of the scientific subject matter, the ability to apply sound scientific judgment, and the ability to perform complex data analysis. NON-STANDARD WORK SCHEDULE, TRAVEL OR ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS This role requires flexibility in work schedule to support time-sensitive fermentation and cell culture experiments. Occasional work outside of core business hours, including weekends, may be required based on experimental timelines and program needs. Work Location Assignment: On Premise The annual base salary for this position ranges from $60,200.00 to $100,400.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 7.5% of the base salary. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility. Candidates must be authorized to be employed in the U.S. by any employer. U.S. work visa sponsorship (such as TN, O-1, H-1B, etc.) is not available for this role now or in the future. cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate Scientist, Vaccines Upstream Bioprocess Development — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Scientist, Vaccines Upstream Bioprocess Development opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Manager of Data Engineering & Delivery (Data Science Production Engineering)
jobs.description: This is an exciting opportunity to lead a Data Engineering & Delivery (DED) team at Natera, a global leader in precision medicine and genomics testing. As a Manager of the DED team inside our Data Science Production Engineering (DSPE) department, you will have the opportunity to work with Natera's diverse and ultra-large data sets (up to PB size), develop innovative solutions with the latest information and cloud technologies, and make real impact by providing timely, accurate, and robust data products and data delivery/automation systems to support Natera's Lab Operations and Genetic Counselor/Lab Director teams, and ultimately impact patients' medical outcomes. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Leadership Lead a Data Engineering & Delivery (DED) team, collectively develop and maintain the data infrastructure, data ingestion solutions, ETL pipelines, robust data products, and data delivery solutions, for both production support and DSPE internal applications. Manage the Data Engineering & Delivery (DED) team, to achieve the timely and efficient delivery of robust data products and systems that can meet DSPE business needs and project requirements. Measure, report, and maintain/improve operational effectiveness. Train and coach team members on new technologies, procedures, and guidelines/best practices. Technical Lead the Data Engineering & Delivery (DED) team, collectively develop and maintain the data infrastructure, data ingestion solutions, ETL pipelines, robust data products, and data delivery solutions, for both production support and DSPE internal applications Translate DSPE's business needs and project requirements into technical specifications and implementation plans. Working with DSPE leadership teams, create design documents that can be efficiently implemented and maintained, for data system architecture, data ETL pipeline, data delivery solution, and other data systems/tools/components. Contribute to key development, testing, deployment, validation, maintenance, and update activities on data products and data systems/tools/components, as well as data delivery tasks. Quality, Compliance, and Documentation Improve and enforce operating procedures for compliance, quality, and efficiency. Create training materials, and contribute to training activities, on DSPE Data Engineering & Delivery (DED) team owned data products and data systems. Cross-Functional Engage proactively and directly with internal and external stakeholders to align development roadmaps, resolve dependencies, and exchange performance metrics. Represent the Data Engineering & Delivery (DED) team in stakeholder meetings. QUALIFICATIONS: Masters degree in Statistics, Data Science, Bioinformatics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Management Science, Operational Research, or other related fields. Doctorate degrees are a plus. Minimal 5 years of relevant industry experience for candidates with a Master's Degree. Minimal 2 years of relevant industry experience for candidates with a Doctorate degree. Minimal 2 years of working experience in a highly regulated environment, e.g., CLIA and/or FDA compliant settings. Minimal 2 years of management experience leading a Data Engineering team, a Data Production/Delivery team, or a Data Analytics team, with demonstrable evidence of leadership and team management skills. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Strong proficiency in SQL and Python programming languages. Proficiency in R is a plus. Proficiency in data analysis and statistical techniques. Proficiency in data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, AWS QuickSight). Strong SQL skills in developing robust and maintainable queries to extract and/or aggregate data from complex data sources. Attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy. Proficiency in building data products, e.g., data aggregation, extraction, transformation, and QC. Past working experience in dbt is a plus. Excellent problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities. Working knowledge of genomics and bioinformatics workflows. Human genetics knowledge is a plus. Proficiency in Git workflow and version control systems like GitHub and/or GitLab. Working experience with healthcare data, electronic health records (EHR), and clinical terminology is a plus. Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment. Good documentation practices and coding style. Strong verbal and written communication skills. Strong interpersonal skills. Strong integrity. Compensation & Total Rewards This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations. This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including: Annual performance incentive bonus Long-term equity awards Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision) 401(k) with company match Generous paid time off and company holidays Additional wellness and work-life benefits Compensation Range $139,900 — $174,900 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! For more information, visit www.natera.com . Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Tech Product Manager, Events and Meetings opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure)
jobs.description: Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast. RESPONSIBILITIES - Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost. - Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load. - Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers. - Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested. - Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back. - Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works. - Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice. - Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure. - Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team. QUALIFICATIONS We expect you to have real depth in most of these: - Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them. - Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count. - Terraform mastery. You've designed module structures, managed state across many accounts, and run large refactors and imports without taking production down. - Strong networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing, routing). - You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it. - Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter. - A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes. - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you. ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE - Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets. - Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF. - GitOps and progressive delivery: Argo CD, Flux, or similar. - Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK, SOC 2 or similar controls. - Running stateful systems in production: Postgres, Redis, or search engines like Vespa or Elasticsearch. - Multi-cloud or neocloud operations (GCP, CoreWeave, or similar). - FinOps: cost attribution, Savings Plans and reservations, and making infrastructure cheaper without making it fragile.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, GPU Cluster Infrastructure)
jobs.description: Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads. RESPONSIBILITIES - Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure. - Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs. - Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints. - Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet. - Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run. - Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention. - Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap. QUALIFICATIONS We expect you to have real depth in most of these: - Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply. - You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE). - You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is. - Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load. - You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++. - You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions. - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you. ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE - Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM. - Slurm or other HPC schedulers. - GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable. - High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production. - Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

Our teams operate at the intersection of innovation and scale, building the infrastructure, partnerships, and capabilities that allow scientists, educators, and innovators to tackle some of the most complex challenges of our time — and to do so with urgency, integrity, and optimism. The Team Our Legal and Grants team (“Team LeGiT”) is a key partner in enabling Biohub’ s pioneering work to combine frontier AI with frontier biology to prevent and cure disease and Learning Commons ’ mission to build AI infrastructure that aligns how students learn with the tools that shape their learning experiences. Team LeGiT helps accelerate Biohub’s and Learning Commons’ missions by structuring, negotiating and executing on strategic partnerships, grants and contracts, as well as providing advice that spans IP, technology, exempt org and labor law. We work directly with scientists, engineers and educators in the development of frontier AI models, partnerships with universities, and a wide range of science and education tools and products. In addition to supporting our programmatic colleagues, we regularly collaborate across Executive, Operations, Central Tech and Investments teams to advance the organization’s philanthropic goals. Our team also manages Mark and Priscilla's Family Giving to provide funding for nonprofit organizations, including in the communities where they live and work. At its core, this team exists to build trust — with our partners, our grantees, and the communities we serve — and to help our organizations operate with integrity as we take on some of the world’s most complex challenges. The Opportunity As a Contracts Manager on the Legal and Grants team, you will support contract owners across CZI, including Biohub and Learning Commons, focused on contracts management and negotiation. You will manage, draft, administer, and execute contracts and lead legal operations projects critical to the success of our strategic mission and operational goals. In addition to working with scientists, engineers, educators and operators to help the organization achieve its ambitious missions, you will support contract owners with end-to-end contracts management and provide training, draft enablement documentation, and improve systems and processes related to contracts. cold_email.subject: Interest in Contracts Manager — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Contracts Manager opportunity with Chan Zuckerberg Initiative at Chan Zuckerberg Initiative.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role Glean is looking for an experienced Global Lead, Analyst Relations to own our industry analyst relations program. Reporting to the Director of Communications, you'll be the primary driver of how Glean engages with the research and advisory firms that increasingly shape enterprise AI buying decisions — including Gartner, Forrester, IDC, 451 Research/S&P Global, and emerging firms covering the AI and enterprise search markets. You'll manage Glean's participation in major evaluations like the Gartner Magic Quadrant, Forrester Wave, and IDC MarketScape; run the day-to-day briefing and inquiry calendar; and build durable, trusted relationships with the analysts who cover Glean. This is a hands-on, highly cross-functional role for someone who thrives on ownership, organization, and translating product substance into a sharp external narrative. You Will: Schedule, prepare, and run analyst briefings, inquiries, and advisory engagements with top-tier and emerging research firms (Gartner, Forrester, IDC, 451 Research/S&P Global, Everest Group, Omdia, Futurum, and others). Lead Glean's participation in major industry evaluations — including Gartner Magic Quadrants, Forrester Waves, and IDC MarketScapes — managing RFI/questionnaire responses, coordinating input across Product, Product Marketing, and executives, and fact-checking draft analyst profiles before publication. Identify and prepare the right internal spokesperson for each engagement (executive overview, product deep-dive/demo, or technical briefing), and own supporting briefing materials and talk tracks. Build and execute AR plans tied to major launches and company moments, including analyst objectives, target lists, briefing cadence, and success metrics. Manage analyst firm subscriptions and contracts (seats, renewals, access tiers), serving as Glean's primary point of contact for Gartner, IDC, and other research-firm account teams. Serve as the face of Glean to the analyst community — managing relationships proactively, ensuring smooth handoffs during internal personnel transitions, and responding promptly to inbound analyst requests. Conduct ongoing research on the analyst and competitive landscape to keep target analyst lists and firm coverage maps current. Coordinate analyst participation and logistics at major company and industry events (e.g., Glean:GO, AWS re:Invent, Google Cloud Next), including invite lists and on-site hosting. Draft and distribute analyst-facing communications, including newsletters, product announcement updates, and briefing recaps. Track and report on AR program outcomes — report mentions, positioning, and briefing/inquiry volume — to Product Marketing and Communications leadership. About You: 6+ years of experience in analyst relations, ideally within B2B SaaS or enterprise technology/AI. Bachelor's degree in Communications, Marketing, Business, or a related field Proven track record managing end-to-end participation in major analyst evaluations (Gartner Magic Quadrant, Forrester Wave, IDC MarketScape, or equivalent). Existing familiarity with — or a demonstrated ability to quickly build relationships with — analysts at Gartner, Forrester, IDC, 451 Research/S&P Global, and emerging research firms. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex product and technical capabilities into clear, compelling narratives for analyst audiences. Highly organized program/project manager who can juggle multiple deadline-driven submission cycles, briefing calendars, and cross-functional stakeholders without dropping details. Comfortable prepping and coaching executives and other spokespeople for high-stakes analyst conversations. A proactive, low-ego operator who can run a program independently while partnering closely with Product Marketing, Communications, Product, and executive stakeholders Location: This role is hybrid (4 days a week in our Mountain View or San Francisco office). Occasional travel required for in-person analyst meetings, briefings, and industry events (e.g., Gartner Symposium, major conferences). Compensation & Benefits: The standard base salary range for this position is $172,000 - $198,000 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We’re committed to building and sustaining a diverse, inclusive workplace. We strive to attract and retain people with a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, and we do not discriminate on the basis of gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. #LI-HYBRID AI-First Mindset at Glean: At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. As part of the interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about, design, and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today — prior Glean experience isn't required. jobs.title: Fire Protection Engineer
jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization delivers the infrastructure that powers frontier AI models. Within Infrastructure Delivery, we turn engineering concepts into safe, reliable, and operational AI campuses by working across design, construction, utilities, commissioning, operations, and external partners. The fire protection function establishes the life-safety and property-protection strategy for these campuses. The team connects code requirements and engineering standards to practical design, construction, testing, incident readiness, and long-term operations. About the Role We are seeking a Fire Protection Engineer to lead owner-side fire and life-safety engineering across large-scale data center programs. You will establish design criteria, review complex fire protection systems, coordinate with authorities and delivery partners, and ensure that fire and life-safety requirements remain clear from early design through construction, commissioning, and operational handover. This role requires strong technical judgment across detection, alarm, suppression, smoke control, water supply, emergency response, and code compliance. You will work closely with engineering, construction, safety, security, commissioning, and operations teams to resolve risks quickly without compromising life safety, reliability, or schedule. Key Responsibilities - Develop and maintain fire protection and life-safety design criteria, technical standards, and review requirements for self-build data center campuses. - Review fire protection drawings, specifications, code analyses, fire and life-safety narratives, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, and sequences of operation across all project phases. - Provide owner-side engineering direction for fire detection and alarm, automatic suppression, fire pumps and water storage, smoke control, emergency communication, and related life-safety systems. - Integrate fire protection requirements with architectural, structural, electrical, mechanical, controls, security, hardware, and operational systems. - Partner with code officials, authorities having jurisdiction, insurers, consultants, contractors, and equipment vendors to resolve code interpretations and approval risks. - Support constructability reviews, RFIs, submittals, field inspections, deficiency resolution, and change management during active construction. - Define commissioning, integrated-system testing, acceptance, turnover, and operational-readiness criteria for fire and life-safety systems. - Assess fire and life-safety risks associated with high-density compute, battery and energy-storage systems, generators and fuel systems, utility infrastructure, cooling systems, hazardous materials, and construction activities. - Support incident response, root-cause reviews, corrective actions, and lessons learned, translating operational findings into improved designs and standards. - Maintain clear records of design decisions, code positions, approvals, testing results, open risks, and turnover requirements. - Travel regularly to project sites to support design reviews, field execution, testing, commissioning, and operational readiness. Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Fire Protection Engineering or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience delivering fire and life-safety systems. - 8+ years of fire protection engineering experience supporting data centers, industrial facilities, advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure, or other mission-critical environments. - Strong knowledge of applicable building and fire codes and standards, including IBC, IFC, NFPA requirements, and local authority approval processes. - Technical depth in fire alarm and detection, water-based suppression, special-hazard suppression, fire pumps and water supply, smoke control, egress, and integrated life-safety systems. - Experience reviewing fire protection designs, specifications, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, testing procedures, and commissioning results. - Demonstrated ability to work with authorities having jurisdiction, engineering consultants, contractors, insurers, vendors, and internal stakeholders. - Experience resolving field issues and design changes while maintaining clear code compliance, safety, quality, schedule, and documentation. - Strong written and verbal communication, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to create clarity when requirements or ownership are ambiguous. - Professional Engineer licensure in Fire Protection Engineering, or the ability to obtain licensure in relevant jurisdictions. Preferred Skills - Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density compute environments, or global multi-site infrastructure programs. - Experience with battery rooms, energy-storage systems, generator plants, fuel systems, high-voltage substations, or other campus utility infrastructure. - Familiarity with performance-based design, fire and smoke modeling, quantitative risk assessment, or fire-hazard analysis. - Experience leading integrated testing and coordinating fire alarm, suppression, controls, security, mechanical, and electrical interfaces. - Experience developing reusable standards, design templates, commissioning requirements, and incident-prevention programs across multiple sites. jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI's infrastructure teams design, build, activate, and operate the critical systems that support large-scale AI compute. Field Service Engineering partners across design, construction, commissioning, site operations, hardware operations, and equipment providers to turn complex infrastructure into safe, reliable, and serviceable systems. About the Role We are seeking a senior, field service engineer to build the technical operating model responsible for critical electrical and mechanical infrastructure across our data center portfolio. This is a field-oriented electrical & mechanical engineering role, not a traditional facilities operations position. You will combine deep systems understanding in data center power and cooling systems to aid in SOO, design, maintenance & operability, troubleshooting and other engineering related responsibility around key equipment. The role will include leveraging training and experience to establish standards, develop people, coordinate vendors, and drive issues from design, first principles, first signals through verified resolution. The strongest candidates will have deep expertise in either electrical and mechanical systems and strong working fluency across the other discipline (e.g. controls, business acumen). Remote - travel 50% Key Responsibilities - Lead field support for startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, repair, and reliability improvement across critical data center infrastructure. - Serve as the senior technical owner for transformers, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, PDUs, protection and controls, chillers, cooling towers, pumps, CDUs, CRAH units, and associated control systems. - Diagnose complex failures across power, cooling, controls, and hardware interfaces; distinguish symptoms from root causes and drive corrective actions through validation. - Build the field service operating model, including staffing recommendations, coverage, escalation paths, response expectations, spare-parts strategy, documentation, and performance metrics. - Aid in hiring, development, and coaching other field service engineers and technicians while creating a culture of safety, technical rigor, accountability, and continuous learning. - Partner with design, construction, commissioning, site operations, and hardware teams to improve maintainability, readiness, and lifecycle reliability. - Manage OEM and service-provider relationships, technical escalations, repair plans, warranties, and sustained corrective action. - Establish and improve safe work practices, including lockout/tagout, switching and maintenance procedures, MOPs, SOPs, EOPs, and incident response. - Translate field learning into design feedback, preventive maintenance improvements, training, and reusable standards. Qualifications - 8+ years of hands-on experience supporting critical electrical, mechanical, or electromechanical infrastructure in data centers, industrial facilities, utilities, manufacturing, or similarly complex environments. - Deep technical expertise in at least one discipline, electrical or mechanical, with demonstrated ability to troubleshoot across electromechanical and controls boundaries. - Experience building, leading, or materially developing a field engineering, service, maintenance, or technician team. - Demonstrated success leading high-severity troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and reliability improvement. - Ability to read and use one-line diagrams, schematics, P&IDs, sequence-of-operations documents, control diagrams, equipment manuals, and commissioning records. - Strong safety judgment and experience working under formal energization, isolation, maintenance, and change-control procedures. - Clear written and verbal communication with engineers, technicians, vendors, construction teams, and senior stakeholders. - Ability to travel up to 50% and support planned or urgent field activity when required. - Bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Field Specialist opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: Frontier AI labs decide what direction their models need to take before the actual training starts. As a Senior Frontier Data Strategist on Scale's Generative AI team, you'll be a trusted voice in those decisions. You'll partner with research leads and senior stakeholders at the world's leading AI labs to shape the data strategy behind their next generation of models, then design the human-data programs to deliver it. You'll sit where frontier research meets Scale's product roadmap, and you'll be expected to move both. With customers, you'll own senior, technically grounded relationships, anticipate where their research is heading, and bring them new data ideas before they ask. Inside Scale, you'll be a leading voice with our AI Product Managers, ML Research, Delivery Operations, and Engagement Management teams, turning what you learn from customers into product priorities and investment decisions. This is a forward-looking, highly cross-functional role. Our Engagement Managers own customer success for live programs; Frontier Data Strategists own everything that comes before it: spotting the need, designing the program, scoping and forecasting it, and winning the work. As a senior member of the team, you'll set the standard for how Scale does this work and help develop the Frontier Data Strategists around you. What you’ll do: Own relationships with senior research stakeholders at your assigned frontier labs, such as research leads, heads of post-training, and technical leadership, and become a strategic thought partner on their post-training, evaluation, and agent roadmaps. Set the data strategy for your accounts: anticipate needs across research areas, spot where the biggest opportunities are, and build a multi-program plan for how Scale can help. Direct the cross-functional team designing Scale's most complex and novel human-data programs, including work that has no precedent at Scale. Shape Scale's product roadmap by representing your customers in planning with AI Product Managers and ML Research, and by resolving tradeoffs between customer needs and what Scale can build. Bring insights from the frontier (research directions, emerging data needs, capability gaps) back to Scale's leadership and technical teams to guide strategy and investment decisions. Own the pipeline of new opportunities for your accounts. Lead scoping, forecasting, and pricing with Delivery, Growth Operations, and Finance, and see the work through to signed programs and a clean handoff. Mentor Frontier Data Strategists, set the bar for program design and customer engagement, and help build the playbooks the team runs on. What we’re looking for: 3+ years in a technical AI/ML role, such as ML engineering, research, applied science, technical product management, or post-training data work at a lab or data provider. Deep fluency in the LLM training lifecycle, especially post-training: SFT, preference data, reward modeling, RL environments, evaluations, agentic training, etc. A track record of owning relationships with senior technical stakeholders, and of influencing their direction through substance. Evidence of shipping ambiguous, high-stakes technical programs from idea to delivery. Experience influencing a product or research roadmap without direct authority. The ability to read a research paper and form an opinion on what data would improve a given capability, and to defend that opinion to researchers. A degree in CS, engineering, math, physics, or another quantitative field. Ideally you'd have: Hands-on experience designing training data, evals, or RL environments. A graduate degree (PhD, MS) or published research in ML or a related field. Experience at a frontier lab, model developer, or AI data company. Experience mentoring or leading technical teammates, formally or informally. This field-based role offers an exciting opportunity to drive the adoption and growth of Signatera, Natera's personalized, tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) test for molecular residual disease (MRD), with a primary focus on lymphoma. The ideal candidate brings a strong background in hematology/oncology sales, established relationships within academic and community cancer centers, and a passion for advancing precision oncology. You will play a critical role in expanding access to innovative molecular diagnostics, building strategic partnerships with healthcare providers, and supporting improved patient care. Key Responsibilities Drive Sales Growth: Achieve and exceed sales objectives by increasing Signatera adoption, expanding the customer base, developing new accounts, and maximizing revenue opportunities throughout the territory. Develop and Execute Territory Strategy: Create and implement a comprehensive territory business plan focused on account acquisition, customer retention, market expansion, and sustainable revenue growth. Engage Key Clinical Stakeholders: Build and strengthen relationships with academic hematologists, medical oncologists, pathologists, and key decision-makers within academic medical centers and community oncology practices. Establish Strategic Partnerships: Collaborate with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), institutional stakeholders, and clinical teams to support care pathway development, institutional partnerships, and EMR integration opportunities. Serve as a Clinical and Product Resource: Develop expertise in Signatera, molecular diagnostics, hematologic malignancies, the oncology patient journey, competitive offerings, and reimbursement dynamics to effectively communicate the clinical value of Natera's solutions. Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Partner with solid tumor-focused Clinical Oncology Specialists (COS), Associate Clinical Oncology Specialists (ACOS), Medical Affairs, and internal teams to strengthen account relationships, address operational challenges, and support customer success. Optimize Account Performance: Identify opportunities to increase test utilization, improve workflow efficiency, resolve missing information (MI) issues, and maximize account growth and retention. Execute Commercial Initiatives: Implement strategic sales and marketing initiatives, identify market opportunities, and leverage business insights to drive adoption across academic and community oncology settings. Qualifications Bachelor's degree required. 5+ years of successful sales experience in hematology/oncology, molecular diagnostics, surgical oncology, or a closely related healthcare field. Demonstrated track record of meeting or exceeding sales goals, developing new business, and growing complex territories. Strong understanding of academic and community oncology markets, clinical workflows, precision medicine, and reimbursement dynamics. Experience engaging hematologists, medical oncologists, pathologists, and other oncology decision-makers strongly preferred. Knowledge of lymphoma, hematologic malignancies, and molecular diagnostic testing highly desirable. Ability to travel approximately 50–75% throughout the assigned territory. Valid driver's license and safe driving record required. Skills & Competencies Exceptional relationship-building, communication, and presentation skills, with the ability to engage both clinical and executive-level stakeholders. Strong business acumen with a strategic, data-driven approach to territory management and account development. Ability to translate complex clinical and scientific information into compelling value propositions. Highly motivated, results-oriented self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced, evolving environment. Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Proven ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams. cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Oncology Specialist, Lymphoma opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

Alongside the models and tools we build for scientists, Anthropic’s life science research teams now run their own wet lab experiments. We’re hiring a life sciences patent counsel to work side-by-side with our researchers as they work to advance biomedical progress. You will manage patent strategy and filings for our life sciences research, from the first conversation with a scientist through global prosecution. You will also be our in-house expert on the patent questions, many of them new, that arise when scientists use AI as a research tool. You will partner closely with our patents lead (direct manager), the Head of IP, Research Legal, our Life Sciences Counsel, and outside counsel to design and implement a patent program that supports our researchers and partners and is aligned with the company’s mission. Responsibilities Manage patent strategy and filings for Anthropic’s life sciences research in the U.S. and internationally, including invention harvesting, filing decisions, drafting oversight, prosecution, and management of outside counsel Serve as the trusted patent advisor to our life science research teams, and design and implement scalable guidance and processes to support our fast-growing life science efforts Make inventorship determinations for AI-assisted research, and advise on inventor declarations and the duty of candor Develop claim and filing strategies across biological and chemical inventions, platform technologies, and computational methods, accounting for written description, enablement, eligibility, and obviousness Partner with Research Legal and Communications on the timing of publications, preprints, presentations, and open-source releases Advise on the patent aspects of agreements with life science and biopharma counterparties, including ownership of inventions and improvements, and support patent diligence and freedom-to-operate analyses for our research Anticipate emerging legal developments affecting AI technologies in the life science and biopharma space and provide strategic guidance to leadership Minimum qualifications Hold a law degree (JD, LLB, or equivalent) and meet the local licensing requirements to work as in-house counsel where you'll be based A degree or equivalent training in a life sciences or chemistry field (for example, molecular biology, biochemistry, genetics, bioengineering, or organic chemistry) Substantial hands-on experience drafting and prosecuting U.S. life sciences patent applications, and directing foreign prosecution through local counsel Lead responsibility for a patent portfolio, including managing budget and outside or foreign counsel Experience making inventorship determinations and resolving ownership questions in multi-party research arrangements (for example, with universities and other partners) Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate legal risk into practical guidance for scientists, researchers, and business partners A low-ego, high-empathy orientation and a “doer” attitude: willing to roll up your sleeves and pitch in where needed Intense curiosity about AI and science, and a commitment to responsible AI development Preferred qualifications 10+ years of patent experience (including time as a patent agent, technical specialist, or examiner) at a law firm, a biotech or pharmaceutical company, or both, with the ability to operate independently and hit the ground running Advanced degree in a life sciences or chemistry field Experience with AI/ML companies, or with inventions at the boundary of biology and machine learning Working knowledge of how patents interact with regulatory exclusivity, trade secrets, and open science Familiarity with biosecurity, dual-use research, or export control considerations in the life sciences Experience leveraging AI to optimize their work, with a desire to work in a fast-paced, innovative environment The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $335,000 — $385,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.description: About the Team The DoorDash Air team is bringing drone delivery to reality. To make this happen, we’re building a strong electrical team to design high reliability, high power density converters, and fault-tolerant controls electronics. Come join us to build a new class of aircrafts and deploy at scale. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike. We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact. We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries. As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries. We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better. About the Role We're hiring a Senior UTM Engineer who will build core components of DoorDash Air's internal route planning and airspace deconfliction stack — the systems that decide where our aircraft can safely fly, coordinate that with other operators and airspace authorities, and keep our internal stakeholders and external systems talking to each other in terms they understand. This is a role for someone who has already lived through the full lifecycle of a distributed, interoperable, uptime-critical system in a field where getting it wrong has real consequences — aviation, finance, communications, healthcare, or similar — and wants to bring that judgment to a fast-moving aerial delivery network. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Design, build, and deploy interoperable services that must pass rigorous, often open-source, conformance and integration testing against external systems and partners. Develop novel path planning and airspace deconfliction algorithms that find safe, efficient routes through real-world, dynamic environments. Build tools that help our teams and systems evaluate and optimize airspace efficiency and utilization. Design integrations that connect the deconfliction stack to existing DoorDash systems, translating mission and airspace status into terms internal stakeholders can act on. Collaborate closely with systems engineering, commercial operations, and flight operations to ship features that hold up in real-world flight. Represent DoorDash Air externally — engaging with peer companies, working groups, and standards bodies to improve interoperable deployments industry-wide and help shape the We’re excited about you because… Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field. You have 5+ years of experience across the full lifecycle — design, build, deployment, and operation — of distributed systems in aviation, finance, communications, healthcare, or another field where interoperability, uptime, and (ideally) safety criticality are core drivers of the work. You've built and shipped production services that had to interoperate with systems you didn't control, including passing external or open-source conformance/certification testing. You have hands-on experience with path planning, routing, or deconfliction problems in real-world, dynamic environments — or the algorithmic depth to pick this up quickly (graph search, optimization, or motion planning fundamentals). You're comfortable building evaluation and analysis tooling, not just the systems being evaluated — you like giving other teams visibility into system performance and efficiency. BS/MS/PhD in CS, EE, Aerospace, Robotics, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Experience with real-time or embedded systems, or with systems that must degrade gracefully under partial failure. cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Systems Business Analyst — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Systems Business Analyst opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Sr Phlebotomist - Washington, DC
jobs.description: This is not a remote position. This position is located in Friendship Heights NW, Washington DC. A minimum of 5 years of phlebotomy experience is required. POSITION SUMMARY A Sr Phlebotomist serves patients by identifying the best method for retrieving blood; preparing specimens for laboratory testing; and performing screening procedures. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES Verifies test requisitions by comparing information with nursing station log; bringing discrepancies to the attention of unit personnel. Verifies patient by reading patient identification. Obtains blood specimens by performing venipunctures and finger sticks. Maintains specimen integrity by using aseptic technique, following department procedures; observing isolation procedures. Tracks collected specimens by initialing, dating, and noting times of collection; maintaining daily tallies of collections performed. Maintains quality results by following department procedures and testing schedule; recording results in the quality-control log; identifying and reporting needed changes. jobs.title: Staff Product Designer, Activation
jobs.description: At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it. We are seeking a Staff Product Designer for the Activation team in our Self-Serve group. For a startup, getting SOC2 and ISO compliant is often the first serious security milestone, and it can stall for months. Activation exists to change that: we want every startup that signs up for Vanta to reach audit-ready in days, not months with an AI. The Activation team is responsible for helping customers get key value out of the product after they purchase. When customers get that value, they're more likely to retain and grow. Activation is an experimentation team, an execution team, and a collaborative platform team - influencing how the rest of the company does growth and designs for a consistent growth experience. As the Staff Product Designer on Activation, you'll set the experience vision for how customers get compliant with Vanta and you'll carry it from strategy to shipped product. You'll own work that spans multiple quarters, shape the roadmap with your PM and engineering partners, and set direction in a space where the right answer isn't obvious yet. You'll proactively champion craft, best growth experience practices, and a data centric approach to design. You'll also document the strategy and lead the room: sometimes authoring briefs that define our bets, and running stakeholder forums that keep large initiatives moving. You will report to a Design Manager on the Self-Serve design team, within Vanta's Experience Design organization. What you’ll do as a Staff Product Designer at Vanta: - Set the end-to-end experience vision for Activation, from first login to to activation and turn it into a roadmap work your squad can ship cycle by cycle. - Act as a key driver of product shape and roadmap alongside your PM and EM, bringing a clear design point of view backed by customer evidence and data. - Design agent-first experiences: decide what the Vanta Agent does on its own, where people review and approve, and how the product earns trust at each step. - Create new, reusable AI patterns and extend existing ones, so other teams can build guided, agentic experiences faster and more consistently. - Define the activation outcomes your work is accountable for, partner with Data to instrument them, and run the experiments and iterations that move them. - Lead customer discovery with cross functional partners and lean engineering teams and share what you learn with leadership in a clear, compelling narrative. - Align partner teams so growth experiences feel like one product, not an org chart. - Document the product strategy for your area: write briefs, and POV docs that frame the problem, the bet, and the plan, so partners can make decisions without you in the room. - Drive large, multi-team initiatives from kickoff to launch in partnership with your Activation squad: set up and run recurring reviews and working sessions with key stakeholders, track decisions and dependencies, and keep everyone aligned as plans change. - Raise the quality bar for interaction, visual, and content craft across Self-Serve through critique, mentorship, and close partnership with engineering through launch. - Help grow the design team by mentoring other designers and helping uphold the hiring bar. How to be successful in this role: - 8+ years of experience designing and shipping high-quality B2B SaaS products, including work that spans multiple teams and quarters. - A track record of designing for business outcomes such as activation, onboarding completion, time-to-value, or retention, and the ability to say where the number started and where it landed. - Experience shipping AI-powered or automation-heavy products, with a strong point of view on how people and agents should work together. - Proven ability to set direction in ambiguous, high-stakes problem spaces: you frame the problem, write the brief, make principled tradeoffs, and bring a clear position to the table. - Strong written strategy skills. You've authored product briefs, strategy docs, or roadmaps that leadership used to make real decisions. - Experience leading large-scale, cross-functional initiatives, including running the recurring meetings, reviews, and rituals that keep many stakeholders aligned and work moving. - Fluency with product analytics and experimentation. You define success metrics, design tests, and change course based on results, including the ones you didn't want. - Exceptional interaction, visual, and content craft on dense, complex product UI, plus experience building patterns that scale across teams. - Strong storytelling and communication skills. You can align a squad, partner teams, and executives around a direction, and keep momentum through setbacks. - Experience working through and alongside other designers to deliver larger efforts, and a habit of mentoring and giving candid, useful feedback. - A portfolio is required, showing end-to-end product work, the reasoning behind key decisions, and the outcomes it delivered. - Experience with product-led growth, onboarding, or guided-setup experiences, especially for small teams or founders. - Experience designing agentic workflows, conversational interfaces, or human-in-the-loop review flows. - Comfort prototyping in code or with AI tools to test ideas quickly with customers and partners. - Familiarity with security, compliance, or GRC. It helps, but it isn't required: many of our designers learned the domain on the job. - Uses AI in day-to-day work to amplify their skills and strengthen their outcomes, applying it across routine workflows, actively building fluency through experimentation, and exercising sound judgment to ensure AI-assisted work meets a high quality bar. What you can expect as a Vanta’n: - Industry-competitive salary and equity - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee-only benefit premiums covered for most medical plans - 16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents - Health & wellness stipend - Remote workspace, internet, and cellphone stipend - Commuter benefits for team members who report to the SF and NYC office - Family planning benefits - Matching 401(k) contribution with immediate vesting - Flexible PTO policy, plus 80 hours of Sick Time - 11 company-paid holidays - Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events! - Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney To provide greater transparency to candidates, we share base pay ranges for all US-based job postings regardless of state. We set standard base pay ranges for all roles based on function, level, and country location, benchmarked against similar-stage growth companies. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors and may vary based on candidate location, skills, depth of work experience, and relevant licenses/credentials. #LI-remote At Vanta, we are committed to hiring diverse talent of different backgrounds and as such, it is important to us to provide an inclusive work environment for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply. About Vanta We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. From our early days automating security monitoring for compliance standards like SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 to creating the world's leading Trust Management Platform, our vision remains unchanged. Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that's real-time and transparent. Referral Instructions If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

Our efforts enable life-changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients. Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible. Position Summary: In this cross functional Quality role, the Product Complaint Analyst 2 will be responsible for processing complaints related to on-market medical devices. Participate in complaint handling activities, such as complaint record review and closure and participate in escalated complaint investigation, as needed, as part of Illumina’s Quality Complaint Handling Unit. This position is responsible for processing complaints which includes, documenting, evaluating and facilitating cross functional discussions with SMEs and ensuring that customer feedback is appropriately evaluated. Provide colleagues support as needed. Responsibilities: Conduct review of complaints for regulated products in a timely manner. Identify, and triage potential adverse events and/or field actions and escalate to the QA Complaint leadership team in a timely manner Participate in monitoring the QA Complaint Handling inbox and conduct tasks associated with rotational “monitor” activities Ensure adequacy and accuracy of complaint records Support Global complaints for case handling audits, when necessary Complete other activities as assigned All listed tasks and responsibilities are deemed essential functions to this position; however, business conditions may require reasonable accommodation for additional tasks and responsibilities.
